report:
## 1. Source-bound four-way accuracy table
P and Q denote the pinned public README URLs listed in files. All values below are publisher claims, not our hardware reproductions.

| Requested variant / measured artifact | GPQA | MMLU | LiveCodeBench | Accuracy engine, hardware, concurrency and speculation | Exact source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| NVFP4 W4A4-W8A8, `NVFP4/W4A4-W8A8/` | 172/198 | 442/500 | 88/100 | SGLang; one RTX PRO6000; C8; DFlash2 | P97–105; cells P117,122,127; SM `/public_scores`, `/protocol` |
| NVFP4 W4A16, `NVFP4/W4A16/` | 170/198 | 439/500 | 91/100 | SGLang; one RTX PRO6000; C8; DFlash2 | P97–105; cells P115,120,125; SW `/public_scores`, `/protocol` |
| NInfer mixed W4A4-W8A8 text path | 177/198 | 444/500 | 92/100 | Official `Neroued/ninfer`; one RTX PRO6000; C8; NO speculation | P157–170; cells P164,166,168 |
| Q6_K GGUF, `GGUF/Qwen3.8-27B-Coder390-EfficientThink-Q6_K-MTP.gguf` | 174/198 | 448/500 | 91/100 | llama.cpp (`llama-server`); one RTX PRO6000; C4; accuracy-run speculation UNKNOWN | Q104–137; cells Q123,126,129 |

Do not substitute the separate GPTQ INT4 W4A16 row (P206–214) for the requested NVFP4 W4A16. They are different artifacts and protocols.

All four accuracy protocols explicitly specify 100K context, 94208 generated-token cap and no client-side generation timeout; empty answers count wrong, truncated-but-correct answers count correct, and failures remain in the denominator (P97,P157,Q104). Preserve the published `100K` label rather than inventing an exact launch configuration: 102400 appears in NInfer performance/recommended commands (P349,799) and Q6 recommended slot arithmetic (Q202), not in a retained accuracy-run command. C8/C4 are request concurrency, not tensor-parallel degree. The accuracy setups are single-GPU, not the proposed local TP2 deployment; explicit TP/PP launch settings are unknown. Blackwell is explicitly named in the corresponding performance sections (P247,349,796; Q174); those details do not turn these into V100 measurements.

## 2. Dates, versions, sampling and evaluator details

- NVFP4 accuracy run start/end dates: UNKNOWN. SM `/stats_updated_at` is `2026-10-05T12:35:40+08:00`; SW is `2026-10-05T10:15:03+08:00`. These are statistics-update timestamps, not asserted run timestamps.
- NInfer mixed accuracy date: `2026-10-05` (P157,241). Exact engine version/commit: UNKNOWN. `Neroued/ninfer` is the engine identity. Do not assign the later vision-check commit to it.
- Q6 accuracy date: UNKNOWN. llama.cpp version/commit: UNKNOWN. Q202 says an upstream build supporting `--spec-type draft-mtp` is required for recommended use, not which build produced the accuracy scores.
- NVFP4 accuracy SGLang version/commit: UNKNOWN. P414's `SGLang >=0.5.19` is a compatibility requirement. P238's `SGLang 0.5.21` belongs to a separate 2026-10-09 six-prompt, FP8-body draft check, not this accuracy run.
- NVFP4 published sampling defaults: `do_sample=true, temperature=1, top_p=0.95, top_k=20` (P474 and the pinned `NVFP4/W4A16/generation_config.json`). The primary tree lists identical generation-config SHA256 for W4A16 and mixed. Per-request sampling overrides and generation seed are UNKNOWN. The config's `transformers_version=5.17.0` is not the SGLang version.
- NVFP4 GPQA reasoning effort is explicitly `xhigh` in both GPQA summary files. Accuracy MMLU/LCB effort is not explicitly recorded in the inspected summaries. NInfer accuracy effort/sampling/seed: UNKNOWN; P349's xhigh/T1/p.95/k20 applies to its performance table. Q6 accuracy effort is explicitly xhigh (Q104); temperature/top_p/top_k, generation seed and whether MTP was enabled for accuracy remain UNKNOWN. Do not import Q174 speed sampling or Q382–392 recommended MTP flags into Q104's accuracy protocol.
- NVFP4 DFlash2 draft length for accuracy: UNKNOWN. Eight draft tokens are documented in recommended performance launch commands, not a retained 100K accuracy command.

`evaluation/NVFP4_MIXED_gpqa.results.summary.json`, `evaluation/NVFP4_W4A16_gpqa.results.summary.json`, `evaluation/NVFP4_MIXED_mmlu.results.summary.json`, `evaluation/NVFP4_W4A16_mmlu.results.summary.json`, `evaluation/NVFP4_MIXED_lcb.results.summary.json`, `evaluation/NVFP4_W4A16_lcb.results.summary.json`, `evaluation/BENCH_NVFP4_MIXED.json`, `evaluation/BENCH_NVFP4_W4A16.json`, and `NVFP4/W4A16/generation_config.json`. NInfer/Q6 code-case timeout and private-case policy remain UNKNOWN.
- Accuracy artifact identity is pinned; historical engine/model/draft runtime commit and full commands are not. Pinning today's README is not recovering those missing runtime pins.

## 3. Q6 binding and package/addition boundaries

Q6 is sourced, not absent: Q104 explicitly says the full triple was run ONLY on the GGUF; Q158 carries those same scores over to its NInfer conversion, and Q479 explicitly says the converted NInfer package was not independently evaluated on the full sets. Q137/Q475 attribute the NInfer LCB attempt's non-JSON replies to evaluator/API incompatibility. Attribute that diagnosis to the publisher; do not convert it into a measured NInfer accuracy failure, success or V100 result.

Q6 GGUF and NInfer share the publisher's stated backbone quantization, but their MTP heads are not the same format: GGUF MTP is Q8_0; NInfer MTP attention/MLP is Q6_K, input projection Q8_0 (Q157–158,198). Neither package contains DFlash2 (Q206,274). Q274 says embedded NInfer vision was added 2026-10-09 while text/MTP weights stayed byte-identical. Vision checks and MTP TPS do not establish a new full accuracy run.

NInfer mixed's 2026-10-05 no-spec scores were carried forward after adding Q8 MTP, DFlash2 and proposal head; the full triad was NOT rerun (P157,241). V3 vision was added 2026-10-09 without changing text/MTP/DFlash2 weights, per publisher (P484). `NInfer 64492cb` belongs to that one-GPU image check, NOT the 2026-10-05 accuracy run. P806–809 separately says V2 packages contain no vision and were not separately evaluated, only SHA256-checked. Therefore neither V2 nor a derived repack inherits a measured V100 accuracy claim.

NVFP4 packages include BF16 MTP and vision (P222,224,407), but their published accuracy used DFlash2, not MTP (P97,474). P238 documents a 2026-10-08 change from per-tensor to block-scaled DFlash2 and a separate 2026-10-09 short check; other DFlash2 speed figures used the old draft. Do not describe historic scores/speeds as freshly rerun with the currently bundled draft. Exact accuracy-draft file hash is UNKNOWN.

## 5. Speed protocols are separate from accuracy

- NVFP4 W4A16/mixed TPS tables: one RTX PRO6000 Blackwell96GB, SGLang, context32768, output cap4096, thinking on, model-default sampling; C1/C4/C8/C16 with 4/12/24/48 requests; no-spec, MTP and DFlash2 measured separately (P247,268–344). P414–472 gives matching recommended performance launches: MTP EAGLE steps3/topk1/draft4; DFlash2 draft8. BENCH JSON distinguishes total-output/wall-time aggregate_tps from median per-request decode TPS. Benchmark date, exact SGLang version and timeout policy are UNKNOWN.
- NInfer mixed TPS: one RTX PRO6000 Blackwell, official NInfer; max-context102400, shared KV819200, max-concurrency8, fp8 KV; output cap4096; xhigh, temperature1/top_p.95/top_k20; C1/C4/C8 with4/12/24 requests; MTP draft4 or DFlash2 draft8 with lm-head-draft; no-spec separately; reported metric is aggregate decode TPS (P349–361). Exact version/date/timeout are UNKNOWN. P361 explicitly warns that engine/context differences make SGLang comparisons reference-only.
- Q6 quick TPS: one RTX PRO6000 Blackwell; stated one-minute quick benchmark; cap512, xhigh, temperature1/top_p.95/top_k20; C1/C2/C4/C8 issue only1/2/4/8 requests; metric all output tokens divided by wall time. NInfer used context32768/shared KV32768/rk8v4/max-concurrency8, Q6 MTP draft3 (Q174,178). Q6 llama.cpp MTP is separately tabulated, but exact speed-run draft length/context, versions and date are UNKNOWN; do not replace with later recommended commands. One-minute quick-test wording is not a documented client timeout. This is not a long-context sustained-capacity or accuracy test (Q174–192,479).

## 6. Comparability conclusion for publication

[ANALYSIS] W4A16 versus mixed NVFP4 is the strongest within-publisher accuracy comparison: same stated SGLang/DFlash2/single-GPU/C8/cap policy, same GPQA dataset/runner hash, both 5-shot MMLU500, and both fixed-ID LCB100 with matching evaluator arguments. Missing exact engine/runtime pins and stochastic rerun uncertainty still preclude a robust global ranking.

[ANALYSIS] NInfer mixed and Q6 can appear alongside them only with protocol columns visible: different engines, no-spec versus DFlash2, C4 versus C8, unknown Q6 accuracy speculation/sampling, and incomplete evaluator binding. Q6's NInfer row is an inherited GGUF claim, not a fourth engine accuracy measurement. Baseline FP8 columns are also reference-only: publisher used two RTX PRO6000 cards with C8 per GPU (P105,109; Q108), not a demonstrated TP2 setup.

[ANALYSIS] Do not rank overall intelligence from a few score differences, transfer publisher scores to 1Cat TP2/V100, claim vision quality from text benchmarks, or compare speed tables as if they shared context, output length, workload size, draft revision and metric definition. No confidence intervals or repeated-run distributions are supplied; publisher explicitly notes MMLU sampling variation (P919,Q480).
